event.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 7?
event.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: The market's overwhelming consensus on 28°C as Munich's highest temperature for September 7 stems from verified observational data and high-resolution forecast models confirming a daytime peak under stable high-pressure conditions with light southerly flow and minimal cloud cover. This value exceeds the 1991–2020 seasonal average high of 21°C, driven by enhanced solar heating and warm advection typical of early September patterns. European models showed tight agreement on maximums near this threshold, with surface observations from stations like Munich Airport aligning closely. Scenarios that could realistically alter resolution remain limited to minor station-specific discrepancies or final quality-control adjustments by the Deutscher Wetterdienst, though current convergence makes significant revisions improbable.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus at 100% implied probability for a 25°C high in London on September 7, 2026, stems from official meteorological observations and model consensus showing peak afternoon temperatures under partly cloudy skies with moderate westerly winds.** 

National weather services and ensemble forecasts, including GFS data, aligned on a maximum of 25°C during the warmest hours, consistent with September climatology for southern England where daily highs in early autumn often range 18–24°C. Real-time station readings and short-range updates reinforced this outcome as the day progressed, with minimal precipitation risk supporting stable thermal conditions. 

While forecast models carry inherent uncertainty from local microclimates or measurement revisions across stations, the strong convergence of data leaves little room for deviation unless unexpected observational adjustments occur before final verification.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent heavy rainfall and widespread cloud cover from a nearby low-pressure system and associated frontal activity have kept Tokyo's daytime temperatures suppressed throughout September 7, 2026, aligning with the market's near-certain 24°C outcome. Official monitoring and numerical weather models indicate maximum readings reached or approached this value amid rain-cooled boundary layers and limited solar insolation, consistent with typical late-summer patterns where precipitation reduces diurnal warming. Historical climatology for early September in the region shows similar conditions often cap highs near seasonal averages when organized rain occurs. Only a rapid clearing of skies or unexpected shift in steering winds could push readings higher, though current observational trends and model consensus make such deviations improbable before resolution.
